input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (Harmony Games). Written 1 October 2025 by Julia Lawson, for the build start on 3 November 2025.

This brief describes the game as it is today. We are reviewing the core gameplay during the pause. If the core changes, we will redo the affected part of this brief with you in November.

1. Scenario
We picked Scenario 1: the core-mechanic playable, showing the basic gameplay in its simplest and most authentic form.
What it is for: we are optimising for player quality and retention, not cheap installs. The playable should filter out people who won't enjoy the real game, while staying true to it, so first tests give clean, reliable results.
How it plays: the player can pick any items freely and make as many matches as they are good enough to make. It is not on rails like the Domino Delights playable.
Build it as the board-editable version you offered: the eight items below are the default board, and we can swap in extras to test. Keeping control over how many zombies and items are on the board is useful to us.

2. Board items
The default board is these eight items:
- Grenade (Survival)
- Couch (Living Room)
- Plushie Chick (Toys) - the item you called "the duck" in the reference level
- Shuriken (Survival)
- Cute Axe (Survival)
- Gift Box (Toys)
- Cactus Plant (Garden) - new colour versions are coming, see the hand-off list
- Bow (Toys) - as it is now, without an arrow
Every other board item on the hand-off list is an extra you can swap in. That includes Couch and Pillow and Plushie Bunny from the reference level, and Dynamite, which was on an earlier version of the list.
Weapon: the Cannon, which is what you've been calling the rocket launcher, sent with its projectile in the first zip on 24 September.
Background: the background from the reference level, sent in the first zip on 24 September.

3. Zombies and animation
Use these four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player.
Use one animation: walk.
All four are in the Unity package Brian sent on 26 September, so you can re-rig them in Spine from that. We can add more zombies later if size and scope allow.

4. Winning and losing
The board is a physics pile of 3D items. The player drags items into a tray that has 7 slots. Any 3 matching items in the tray clear, and each cleared match fires that item at the zombies.
Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
Lose: the zombies reach the player and the player's HP runs out. The loss screen only appears at zero HP.
A full tray is not a loss: if all 7 slots fill without a match, the tray clears and the surviving zombies enrage (they get tougher), but play continues. It is a tempo penalty, not a fail state.
Different items hit zombies differently: for example the grenade is powerful, the couch does splash damage, and the plushie is weak but funny.
The reference level we built on 23 September, which Brian recorded and sent you on 24 September, shows all of this.

5. Sound
You can use these now; they are ours to hand over:
- Matching sound
- Success sound
- Failure sound
Still to come from us:
- Background music: a new track made for the ad (not the in-game track), being cut down to a loop.
- Rocket sound and explosion sound: the current ones come from a sound library and a bought sound pack. They stay with us until we have our own versions, so please don't use the sounds from the game build. We will send our own versions.
Music: as you told us last time, music may only start after the player's first tap or click.

6. Formats
Your format list from September still applies:
- 3D: .fbx, .glb or .blend. FBX files must be exported as Binary, not ASCII.
- 2D: .png. For 2D animations, character parts must be separated into pieces.
- Fonts: .ttf or .woff2.
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav.

7. Start date
The build starts on Monday 3 November 2025, with the kickoff call that day.

8. What's still coming from us
The hand-off list (a separate sheet, linked in the PlayableX channel) has one row per asset. Each row shows its state:
- Delivered: you have the current file.
- Ready: exported and waiting in our outgoing folder.
- Owed: still with us, with what's owed and who has it.
As of 1 October: 8 Delivered, 68 Ready, 20 Owed.
Of the eight default board items, only the Cactus Plant is still owed, because of its new colour versions. Grenade, Couch and Plushie Chick are delivered. Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box and Bow are ready.

• *Board change:* Robert put the Bow in the eight instead of Dynamite (26 Sep, in #zombie-art). Dynamite is now an extra.
• *Board item still owed:* Cactus Plant is the only one of the eight not ready. Robert got new colour versions of the cactus, chainsaw and cone on 29 Sep, which is after Claire's FBXs were exported, so all three have to go again from Claire.
• *Zombies:* Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player, walk only. That's Robert's pick and it hasn't changed.

Hi team, here's what you need for the ZM3D playable ahead of the 3 November start.

• *Brief* (scenario, the eight board items, the four zombies and the walk animation, win/lose and the 7-slot tray, sound, formats, start date): https://docs.google.com/document/d/99921598485200eaf6965d53/edit

Of 96 assets, 8 are already with you, 68 are exported and ready to send, and 20 are still coming from us. The 20 still coming are:

• Item icons and UI as PNG
• Fonts

The brief is written for the game as it is today. If the core gameplay changes during the pause, we'll redo that part with you in November.
